title: Retailers warn of price rises if Autumn Budget fails to deliver
gist: The British Retail Consortium warns that UK shop price inflation rose to 2.1% in October and will continue rising unless the Chancellor cuts business rates, employment costs, and packaging taxes in the Autumn Budget. Financial distress among British businesses has hit a 20-year high, with 86% of small businesses saying the Budget could further damage their finances.

title: Shop price inflation hits two year high, BRC calls for action ahead of Budget
gist: BRC and NielsenIQ data show UK shop price inflation hit 2.1% YoY in October, a near two-year high, driven by non-food categories like furniture, flooring and DIY, with food ambient inflation also accelerating. The BRC is urging the Chancellor to cancel a 3.5% business rates increase and reduce employment costs ahead of the Autumn Budget.

title: Online retailers not ready for Black Friday, expert warns
gist: An SEO expert warns that e-commerce retailers risk missing Black Friday sales by failing to optimise for AI shopping agents, which are producing 30–40% higher order values among users who rely on them. Key actions include enriching product data, maintaining accurate pricing feeds, implementing structured data, and building third-party credibility signals.

title: Why are brands still discounting blind?
gist: An op-ed by Particular Audience's CEO argues that while retail media has made advertising measurable and adjustable, trade promotions and discounting remain opaque and preset — brands commit to fixed discounts without knowing the minimum needed to convert, giving away unnecessary margin. The piece proposes real-time, SKU-level, contextual discount logic as a direct parallel to retail media's targeting model.

title: Walmart debuts longer Black Friday, Cyber Monday sales events
gist: Walmart is extending its Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales events to 14 days total in 2026, up from 10 days in 2025, spread across three distinct sales windows in November and December. Walmart+ members will get tiered early access to deals, and the retailer has also launched a bundled Walmart+/Sam's Club membership at $120/year.

title: Why returns are becoming a bigger focus for TikTok Shop and DoorDash
gist: TikTok Shop and DoorDash are both investing in frictionless returns as a conversion lever, with DoorDash launching a $7.99 on-demand pickup returns service dispatching drivers within 30 minutes. The trend reflects marketplaces treating easy returns as a competitive differentiator to drive purchase confidence.

title: Glossy+ Research: Brands’ holiday marketing tactics shift in 2026
gist: A Glossy+ Research survey of 90 brand and retailer professionals found that marketing tactics for the 2026 holiday season are shifting compared to 2025, with commerce channel priorities among marketers changing. Full details are behind a paywall.

title: Dollar General sued by FTC over ‘deceptive pricing practices’
gist: The FTC and 20 U.S. states have sued Dollar General for allegedly charging customers higher prices at the register than those displayed on shelf tags and in advertising, with undercover investigations finding pricing discrepancies in every store visited. The retailer has received over 29,000 consumer complaints about the issue since January 2023 but allegedly failed to fix it.

title: Prada launches ChatGPT tool to help shoppers discover luxury products
gist: Prada has launched a ChatGPT-powered conversational tool in the UK, US, and Italy that lets shoppers discover products and find store information through AI dialogue, developed with Accenture Song and DaVinci Commerce.

title: GUEST COMMENT Proving that retail media sales are truly incremental
gist: A Decentriq executive argues that retail media's attributed sales figures systematically overstate real impact because they count high-intent shoppers who would have bought anyway, and lays out how randomised holdouts and privacy-preserving data clean rooms can measure true incrementality.

title: 83% of UK consumers fear rising prices ahead of Budget
gist: Over 80% of UK consumers are worried about rising food prices and inflation ahead of the Budget, as shop price inflation hit 2.1% in October — its highest since February 2024 — with UK retailers collectively facing a £41bn tax bill for 2026/27.

title: How Lush quit social media ads and still drove growth
gist: Lush quit paid social advertising on Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, and Snapchat in 2021 over data privacy and algorithm concerns, and has since maintained only a token presence on those platforms while still driving brand growth.

title: Target overhauls Threshold home goods brand
gist: Target has overhauled its Threshold home goods private label — its largest, at nearly $3 billion annually — by cutting prices on select items, adding 800+ new products, and improving in-store merchandising to help shoppers visualize complementary items together.

title: These 3 department stores need a good holiday
gist: Kohl's, J.C. Penney, and Saks Fifth Avenue (now Exemplar Luxury Group, post-bankruptcy) each face a critical holiday season test in 2026, with analysts scrutinizing their ability to convert holiday traffic into profitable sales and cash flow amid ongoing turnaround struggles.

title: Poundland faces growing insolvency risk as major shareholder rejects solvent rescue proposal
gist: Poundland faces potential insolvency after its controlling shareholder Gordon Brothers rejected a solvent takeover bid, with three sale-process directors reportedly ready to resign amid concerns the shareholder is steering the retailer toward a break-up.

title: Brands Briefing: Shoulder bags and TikTok Shop are powering Vera Bradley’s latest turnaround
gist: Vera Bradley reported its first quarterly revenue growth in nearly five years after refocusing on shoulder bags, personalized bag charms, and investment in TikTok and Instagram as part of its 'Project Sunshine' turnaround plan.

title: DoorDash to Acquire Instacart
gist: DoorDash has announced a deal to acquire Instacart, combining the two largest US on-demand delivery platforms into a single entity. The move would give DoorDash significant reach into grocery and local retail delivery.

title: Budget 2026: What does it mean for UK retailers?
gist: The UK's 2026 Autumn Budget offers retailers some relief through expanded business rates support and lower energy and fuel costs, but a 3.9% National Living Wage rise and frozen National Insurance thresholds keep labour costs high. A notable e-commerce measure makes online marketplaces responsible for collecting VAT on qualifying seller transactions from October 2027.

title: Autumn Budget review: Business rates relief is welcome, but will it save Britain’s struggling high streets?
gist: The UK Autumn Budget raised the Small Business Rates Relief threshold to £18,000, removing around 70,000 businesses from rates, but experts warn that rising minimum wage and frozen National Insurance thresholds could wipe out those savings for most retailers. The OBR forecasts no real earnings growth next year, with inflation expected to offset minimum wage gains.

title: “Smoke and mirrors”: retail reacts to the Autumn Budget
gist: Retail industry bodies gave a mixed-to-negative reaction to the UK Budget, with the British Retail Consortium calling the business rates freeze "smoke and mirrors" and warning it adds £250m to retailers' bills. The VAT enforcement measure targeting marketplace sellers was one of the few broadly welcomed announcements.

title: Retail media’s AI gap: 88% use AI for analysis, but just 16% for product and ad ranking
gist: Live polling at IAB Europe's Retail Media Impact Summit found that while 88% of retail media professionals use AI for data analysis and reporting, only 16% use it to determine product or ad rankings, with trust and control cited as the main barriers. Research by Particular Audience showed AI-driven search identified 80% of the relevant product catalogue within the first 120 results, versus 48.5% for traditional keyword search.

title: Etsy CEO addresses friction of AI vs. human creativity
gist: Etsy CEO Kruti Patel Goyal said AI is being used to improve product discovery while the company simultaneously tightens rules on AI-generated listings, banning AI-produced functional guides and requiring at least one real product image. Q3 GMS rose 8.8% year-over-year to $2.6bn and active buyers grew 1% — the first increase in two years.

title: Retailers are still figuring out how to tie AI goals to executive compensation
gist: Ralph Lauren has added AI performance metrics as a factor in executive annual incentive payouts, a change surfaced in an SEC filing, reflecting a broader retail industry shift toward formalizing AI adoption goals at the leadership level.

title: Fabletics VP of Media & Growth Europe Daniel Klarkowski on why authenticity, AI and influencers are reshaping growth
gist: Fabletics VP of Media & Growth Europe Daniel Klarkowski describes the brand's shift toward micro-influencer networks (1,500+ in Europe), multi-touch attribution, and cautious AI use focused on analytics rather than creative, as CAC rises and platform algorithms make follower counts less predictive of reach. He also flags growing interest in physical retail and offline brand experiences as a counterweight to pure digital dependency.

title: Why Facetheory is betting on Boots, bricks and mortar and British beauty
gist: Skincare brand Facetheory, acquired out of distress in mid-2025, has launched into 224 Boots stores as its first UK physical retail presence, after building a 700,000-strong DTC customer base entirely online over 12 years. Founder Suraj Lalvani frames the move as a deliberate pivot to omnichannel, arguing that no single channel is strong enough and that physical retail drives discovery, trust, and experience that digital cannot replicate.

title: Phase Eight owner confirms customer data accessed in cyber attack
gist: TFG London, owner of Phase Eight, Hobbs and Whistles, confirmed that customer personal data including contact details, order information, and limited payment data was accessed in a cyber attack identified on 11 October. Full payment card details and login credentials were not compromised.

title: Amazon sales rise 12% as AWS growth drives profits
gist: Amazon reported Q3 2026 net sales of $201.9bn, up 12% year-on-year, with operating income rising 61% to $28.1bn and AWS growing 39% to $46bn. North American retail sales grew 6%, with grocery and ultra-fast delivery (Amazon Now) flagged as standout operational performers.

title: Amazon’s Ads nears $20 billion in Q3 as it bets on agentic AI to fuel further growth
gist: Amazon's advertising business generated nearly $20 billion in Q3 2026, up 12% year-on-year, making it one of the company's fastest-growing units, with agentic AI flagged as a key lever for future ad growth.

title: Amazon says more than 400M customers have used Alexa for Shopping in the last 12 months
gist: Amazon reported that over 400 million customers used Alexa for Shopping in the last 12 months, up from 350 million in July, with those users spending 50% more than non-users.

title: Amazon introduces returnless refunds in Europe
gist: Amazon has launched its FBA Returnless Resolutions programme across five European markets (UK, Germany, Italy, France, Spain), allowing sellers to refund customers on items priced up to €75 without requiring the product's return. Sellers bear the inventory loss and returns still count toward their return rate, prompting criticism from some merchants.

title: FTC orders Target, Walmart to provide details in personalized pricing inquiry
gist: The FTC has issued orders to Walmart, Target, airlines, and other companies requiring them to detail how personal data and AI are used to set individualized prices, as part of a broader investigation into personalized pricing practices. Companies have 45 days to respond.

title: The Backroom: Dynamic pricing and the anxious consumer
gist: Retail Dive's podcast episode examines how consumer anxiety about dynamic and personalized pricing — amplified by Walmart's use of digital shelf labels and progressive advocacy — is shaping the pre-holiday retail environment alongside already-fragile consumer confidence.

title: UK retail sales jump in October as shoppers return to winter wardrobes
gist: UK like-for-like retail sales grew 4.6% in October — the strongest since January 2025 — driven primarily by online sales rising 10.1%, while in-store growth was just 2.2%, well below inflation. Analysts caution that the uplift was largely weather-driven catch-up spending.

title: Online sales help October deliver strongest retail sales growth since January 2025
gist: UK October retail sales in discretionary categories rose 4.6% year-on-year — the strongest BDO has recorded since January 2025 — with online up 10.1% versus just 2.2% for physical stores, following an unusually weak September. Analysts attribute the rebound largely to delayed seasonal purchases and promotions activity.

title: Most consumers aren’t using AI for product discovery, yet
gist: Only 10% of U.S. consumers currently start product discovery with AI, though adoption is higher among Gen Z, millennials, and high-income shoppers, according to an AlixPartners survey of 9,000+ consumers. The report warns that poor product metadata will make brands invisible as AI agents grow as a discovery channel.

title: Cotopaxi adopts a drop strategy to build buzz ahead of BFCM
gist: Outdoor brand Cotopaxi is launching 'Cotodays,' a drop-a-product-every-other-day campaign from Nov. 1–11 featuring limited-edition items, deliberately positioning it before the BFCM promotional window to drive engagement without competing on discounts.

title: Big-Box Briefing: What to watch this holiday season as Target, Walmart and more battle for sales
gist: Major brick-and-mortar retailers including Target, Walmart, Kohl's, Best Buy and Macy's have announced their Black Friday and Cyber Monday plans for 2026, signaling the start of the holiday sales battle.

title: Fanatics revamps outfit curation tool with OpenAI
gist: Fanatics has rebuilt its 'Shop the Look' outfit-curation tool in partnership with OpenAI, using team, inventory, and product data to generate daily-refreshed coordinated outfit suggestions on product pages. The revamped tool has driven 10% higher engagement than its predecessor.

title: DoorDash to buy Instacart for $17B
gist: DoorDash has announced plans to acquire Instacart for approximately $17 billion, combining DoorDash's delivery network with Instacart's grocery partnerships, e-commerce technology, and retail media business. The deal is expected to close in late 2027 or early 2028.

title: Poundland moves closer to administration after major shareholder rejects rescue bid
gist: Poundland has filed a Notice of Intention to appoint administrators after its major shareholder Gordon Brothers rejected a solvent takeover proposal from Martin Property Group, giving the 600-store, 12,000-employee retailer a 10-working-day window to find a rescue deal.

title: What Nike’s Jordan pullback means for Foot Locker
gist: Nike is pulling back on retro Jordan product launches to correct oversupply, a move analysts estimate will hit Foot Locker — whose largest wholesale partner is Jordan at ~$1.85bn in sales — with up to $550 million in lost revenue from spring 2027. Foot Locker's parent Dick's Sporting Goods has already lowered the retailer's full-year outlook.

title: Consumer confidence edges up on decline in gas prices: Conference Board
gist: U.S. consumer confidence rose 7.5 points in October to 91.7, the highest since June, driven by a slight decline in gasoline prices, though it remains on a long-term downward trend with consumers still expecting 5.8% inflation in 12 months.

title: Michael Kors finds a new audience on TikTok Shop ahead of Black Friday
gist: Michael Kors launched on TikTok Shop and is seeing sales nearly four times initial expectations, with the channel serving as a discovery and purchase path for Gen Z shoppers who had little prior awareness of the brand.

title: Amazon CEO says retail business is being slept on
gist: Amazon's retail business grew online store sales 2% YoY to $68.5B in Q3, with CEO Andy Jassy highlighting that grocery and everyday essentials are growing three times faster than the rest of the store business, making Amazon stickier for Prime members.

title: Basically no one is using AI agents for their DoorDash orders
gist: DoorDash CEO Tony Xu disclosed that AI agents have generated only 'several hundred' orders total on the platform, compared to nearly 1 billion orders in Q3 alone, suggesting agentic commerce is far from mainstream for simple, habitual purchases.

title: DoorDash said it’s only received ‘several hundred’ orders from AI agents
gist: DoorDash confirmed only several hundred total orders have come through third-party AI agents, while the company is building its own agentic ordering tools and exploring advertising opportunities within third-party agents.

title: Ouai launches cinematic web series as long-form content trends: ‘People are craving a new version of authenticity’
gist: Ouai, a P&G-owned hair care brand, produced a three-part cinematic slasher-comedy web series over nearly a year, framing the investment as a response to consumer appetite for trustworthy, high-craft content amid the rise of AI-generated material.

title: Argos enlists Richard Ayoade for 2026 Christmas advert
gist: Argos has launched its 2026 Christmas campaign featuring Richard Ayoade in a Dickens-inspired ad designed to shift consumer perception of the retailer beyond toys toward tech, beauty, and homeware. The campaign uses nostalgia — pairing catalogue-era products with modern equivalents — to broaden awareness of Argos's current range.

title: WATCH Tesco reunites old friends in 2026 Christmas advert
gist: Tesco's 2026 Christmas ad centers on a story of two old friends reuniting after a grocery delivery mishap, reinforcing its home delivery proposition and 'Every Little Helps' brand platform. The campaign spans TV, social, and in-store experiences including the return of Santa's Grottos.

title: noyb win: French electronics retailer Fnac Darty fined €7M
gist: France's data regulator CNIL fined Fnac Darty €7 million for activating third-party tracking on its mobile app without user consent, confirming the trackers were used to collect browsing history for product recommendations and algorithm training. The fine follows a 2023 noyb complaint and reinforces that consent is a legal prerequisite for personalized advertising, not an optional step.

title: From restaurant guides to payments, here’s how TikTok is building a super app
gist: TikTok is systematically expanding beyond short-form video into restaurant guides, peer-to-peer payments, hotel booking, sports hubs, and casual games, following the 'super app' model pioneered in China by WeChat. TikTok Shop has already reached $15.82B in U.S. sales in 2025, accounting for 18.2% of social commerce, with projections putting it at 24.1% by 2027.

title: What DoorDash’s proposed acquisition of Instacart means for Uber, Amazon and the rest of the quick commerce space
gist: DoorDash has proposed a $17 billion acquisition of Instacart, which would combine two platforms that together account for 77% of U.S. consumer spending on delivery platforms, intensifying competition in quick commerce.

title: Your catalog may already be visible to AI agents. Making it trustworthy is the next step.
gist: Retailers whose product catalogs are discoverable by AI agents still face gaps in catalog data quality, real-time inventory sync, and pricing consistency that reduce the likelihood of AI agents actually recommending their products. Salesforce data shows 41% of multichannel retailers have inconsistent pricing across channels and 40% lack real-time inventory sync.

title: GUEST COMMENT Boxing Day boxes clever: are retailers missing the bigger Q4 sales opportunity?
gist: A Brave Ads analysis argues UK retailers over-concentrate Q4 budgets on Black Friday while underinvesting in Boxing Day and post-Christmas search demand, with Adobe reporting £500M+ in UK online spend on 26 December 2025 alone.

title: M&S, Asos and Topshop turn to celebrity partnerships and AI in high street fashion revival
gist: M&S, Asos, and Topshop are using celebrity partnerships, AI styling tools, and accessible luxury collections to attract younger shoppers, with M&S reporting a 16% year-on-year increase in under-35 customers since adopting more fashion-led ranges.

title: Brussels approves Temu’s action plan
gist: The European Commission has approved Temu's action plan to address illegal product listings, requiring five corrective measures, while a previously imposed fine remains in force.

title: Google search loses its free pass with buyers
gist: Google's AI Overviews are reducing click-through rates on search results, shrinking available ad inventory and pushing up CPCs, leading media buyers to scrutinize Google search ROI more closely heading into Q4.

title: Christmas campaigns 2026: Shoppers want lower prices, so why are retailers betting big on festive storytelling?
gist: UK retailers are launching high-budget Christmas campaigns ranging from emotional storytelling (John Lewis, Sainsbury's) to value-focused spectacle (Asda), even as research shows 57% of shoppers would prefer the money spent on lower prices — and purchase intent from adverts remains hard to prove.

title: Asda appoints former Morrisons boss David Potts as group CEO
gist: Asda has appointed former Morrisons CEO David Potts as its new group chief executive, with Allan Leighton moving to non-executive group chairman; Potts says improving shopping experience and keeping prices low are his immediate priorities.

title: Holiday shoppers only want a dash of AI for the gift hunt
gist: Shoppers are beginning to use AI tools for holiday gift inspiration and price comparison, but most are unwilling to let AI finalize purchases — particularly because of trust concerns around data security and a desire to retain personal control over gifting decisions.

title: DHL introduces fee for second delivery attempt
gist: DHL is introducing a €2.99 fee for second parcel delivery attempts, a change from its previous policy of including re-delivery in the standard service.

title: Could your existing in-store network become a retail media channel?
gist: Retailers with existing in-store digital screen networks can potentially monetize them as retail media channels by layering advertiser campaign management, measurement, and content rules onto infrastructure already in place, rather than building from scratch.

title: Black Friday discount war risks backfiring as UK shoppers cut budgets by a third
gist: UK Black Friday and Cyber Monday spending is forecast to drop 32% to £9.9bn in 2026, with average spend per shopper falling from £390 to £267, while high-spending shoppers retreat significantly — pushing experts to warn against blanket discounts in favor of targeted, margin-conscious promotions.

title: Ad Tech Briefing: Google’s AI-reckoning
gist: Google's Q3 earnings reportedly showed unexpected weakness tied to the rise of its own AI products, raising questions about how AI cannibalizes the digital advertising revenue that funds Big Tech.

title: What DoorDash’s Instacart acquisition says about the modern delivery platform pitch
gist: DoorDash's announced $17 billion acquisition of Instacart reflects how delivery platforms are competing on breadth of services — advertising, AI, and in-store B2B tools — rather than delivery alone.

title: Poundland rescue row intensifies as founder and ministers pile pressure on Gordon Brothers
gist: Poundland is on the verge of administration after owner Gordon Brothers rejected a solvent rescue bid, with the chain's co-founder and UK government ministers publicly pressuring the firm to accept a deal that could protect 11,000 jobs across roughly 600 stores.

title: Consumers want to feel the holiday spirit. A good store experience can help.
gist: With consumers under financial pressure this holiday season, retail experts say the winning in-store strategy is helping shoppers achieve their existing traditions rather than trying to change their behavior — prioritizing fast problem resolution, localized assortments, and motivated store associates.

title: AI recommendations are leading to returns
gist: A Blue Yonder survey of 2,000 U.S. shoppers found that 46% of those who bought an AI-recommended product returned it, most often because the item didn't match its description — a problem the CEO attributes to poor product data, not the AI itself.

title: How Stitch Fix is using AI and customer feedback to build its private brands
gist: Stitch Fix consolidated its private-label portfolio from 16 to 10 brands and expanded each into adjacent categories like footwear and bags, using customer feedback and AI to build brands around actual lifestyle needs rather than product categories.

title: Here are the questions on advertisers’ minds after the DoorDash-Instacart deal
gist: DoorDash's $17 billion planned acquisition of Instacart has media buyers questioning the long-term impact on retail media, though the deal isn't expected to close until late 2027 or early 2028.

title: Omnicom Media joins RMX retail media pilot
gist: SMG has launched RMX, a retail media exchange platform, with Omnicom Media as its beta agency partner, aiming to unify campaign discovery, planning, and reporting across fragmented retail media networks in the UK.

title: M&S fashion and home sales recover but profits remain below pre-cyber attack levels
gist: M&S reported a 17.5% sales rise in its Fashion, Home & Beauty division for H1 2026, but profit and margins remain well below pre-cyber attack levels due to lingering stock availability issues and rising online returns and fulfilment costs.

title: Amazon’s shopping agent now takes orders by text, with Sponsored Product ads in the replies
gist: Amazon's Alexa shopping agent now accepts orders via SMS for an invite-only group of U.S. customers, with Sponsored Product ads appearing inside those text conversations — though purchases the agent completes autonomously remain ad-free.

title: Amazon adds over 100 Alexa for Shopping functions
gist: Amazon has added over 100 new capabilities to Alexa for Shopping, covering registries, subscriptions, delivery, and billing; Amazon's CEO noted that users of the tool spend 50% more per order than non-users.

title: Walmart ramps up Sparky features in time for the holidays
gist: Walmart's AI assistant Sparky added features including shopping-list-to-cart conversion, visual recognition, and recipe generation ahead of the holidays; Walmart says Sparky users spend 40% more per order and usage is up 70% since launch.

title: Zalando sees new revenue potential in external shops
gist: Zalando is expanding its platform to surface products from external shops like Westwing, with an AI shopping agent eventually placing orders on those external sites directly from within the Zalando app.

title: EU Commission approves takeover Ceconomy by JD.com
gist: The European Commission has approved JD.com's acquisition of Ceconomy, owner of MediaMarkt and Saturn, with conditions requiring JD.com to offer warehousing and logistics services to third-party retailers.

title: JD Sports rolls out stock-tracking technology across 414 stores to tackle availability and theft
gist: JD Sports deployed RFID inventory tracking across 414 UK and Ireland stores in roughly three months, achieving 98% on-shelf availability and cutting replenishment times by 20%.

title: GUEST COMMENT Lidl is winning the high street. Can it win the agentic shopping era?
gist: A strategy piece examines how Lidl's physical-first, discount model may fare as AI shopping agents increasingly handle purchase decisions, arguing the retailer must choose between optimizing for agent-driven price comparison or investing in direct consumer relationships that agents can't easily replicate.

title: How TF is the grocery store a media channel?
gist: A sponsored guide from Grocery TV argues the physical grocery store remains a critical purchase-decision environment, citing that 95% of grocery shoppers make at least half their decisions in-store.

title: Hush opens first three standalone stores as it moves onto the high street
gist: UK womenswear brand Hush has opened its first three standalone stores after building its business primarily online, selecting three distinct retail environments to test different customer profiles.

title: Future of Marketing Briefing: Creators had a big year. Christmas still went to the celebrities
gist: Analysis of early holiday ad campaigns finds that despite creator marketing dominating brand strategies throughout the year, major Christmas campaigns from brands like John Lewis and Burberry are still led by celebrities rather than creators.

title: Glossy Pop Newsletter: Depop is hosting over 2,000 campus events this fall
gist: Depop has tripled its campus presence to over 300 colleges and is running more than 2,000 in-person events this fall through its Campus Manager ambassador program, targeting Gen Z sellers and buyers.

title: Big-Box Briefing: The themes that will dominate Jason Bonfig’s tenure as Best Buy’s new CEO
gist: Jason Bonfig, a 27-year Best Buy veteran, became CEO on November 1, succeeding Corie Barry, with his tenure expected to focus on accelerating the company's existing strategy.

title: Russia denies involvement in cyberattacks on supermarket fridges across Europe
gist: A wave of cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration systems across Belgium, Sweden, Ireland, France, and the UK has forced retailers to discard large quantities of perishable food; Russia denied involvement despite two pro-Russian groups claiming responsibility.

title: US government warns of ‘ongoing cyber threat’ amid mass hacks of industrial retail and military freezers
gist: CISA, the FBI, and multiple U.S. federal agencies issued a joint warning about an ongoing cyber threat targeting internet-connected industrial refrigeration systems at grocery stores, cold storage facilities, military bases, and a blood bank, with attacks attributed broadly to Iran by security researchers.

title: How delivery apps came to be ‘discovery platforms’
gist: DoorDash is acquiring Instacart for $17 billion, a move that signals delivery apps like DoorDash, Uber, and Instacart are repositioning themselves as retail discovery platforms rather than pure logistics providers.

title: Bed Bath & Beyond’s new concept takes a page from original format
gist: Neighborhood Intelligence (parent of Bed Bath & Beyond, The Container Store, Kirkland's) is opening a standalone Bed Bath & Beyond store in Arizona, closing underperforming locations, and shifting focus to organic growth and global sourcing to improve margins. E-commerce revenue grew 9%, led by 75% growth from Overstock.com.

title: The Children’s Place shakes up leadership amid bankruptcy rumors
gist: The Children's Place is reportedly considering bankruptcy and possible liquidation, with four senior executives including the interim CEO departing amid declining sales and widening losses.

title: Under Armour to sell more full-price product at outlet stores
gist: Under Armour is restructuring its retail and product strategy—cutting SKUs by another 25%, adding full-price products to outlet stores, and licensing its youth sports category—as revenue fell 7% and analysts question whether the brand has a relevance problem beyond cyclical softness.

title: Reformation implements new AI planning tool, helping in-stock rates
gist: Reformation implemented an AI-backed demand-forecasting and planning tool that improved in-stock rates and full-price selling, contributing to 19% revenue growth in Q3 and an expansion of its active customer base by 23%.

title: As Barbie stumbles, Mattel cuts forecast ahead of the holidays
gist: Mattel posted 4% net sales growth in Q3 but cut its full-year guidance, citing underperformance of the Barbie brand and tariff uncertainty, as its new CEO faces pressure from investors to turn the business around.

title: Ramp data shows AI spending stalling just as Anthropic nears its IPO
gist: Ramp's spending data shows AI token volumes are rising but dollar spend flatlined in August–September, as price competition from OpenAI, Anthropic, and open-source models makes AI usage cheaper even as consumption grows.

title: Inside Oner Active’s tequila-scented new flagship in NYC
gist: Oner Active is opening its first NYC flagship store, with founder Krissy Cela deliberately positioning the brand away from wellness clichés — including a custom tequila-scented store fragrance — to create a distinct in-store identity.

title: Show HN: Coldframe, a honeypot that poses as a supermarket fridge controller
gist: A developer released an open-source Python honeypot that impersonates internet-exposed supermarket refrigeration controllers to log attacker behavior, credentials, and exploit attempts targeting real CVEs in Danfoss and Dixell systems.

title: After the midterms, things are looking rocky for Elon Musk and data centers
gist: Following a Democratic wave in U.S. midterm elections, nearly all ballot measures restricting data center construction passed, and newly elected officials in states like Texas have campaigned on limiting hyperscaler projects, while companies like OpenAI are already adjusting their community engagement policies in response.

title: ThredUp revenue growth slows despite record number of buyers
gist: ThredUp posted 7% revenue growth to $88.2M in Q3 but cut Q4 guidance sharply as average item prices fell from $21 to $18 and competitors ramped up promotions. Record buyer counts and order volumes couldn't offset lower spend-per-item and intensifying pressure from peer-to-peer rivals like Depop.

title: Amazon deploys thousands of smart glasses to delivery drivers
gist: Amazon is deploying 5,000 smart glasses to delivery drivers in 2026, expanding to 20,000+ by end of 2027, with the glasses surfacing navigation, delivery preferences, and proof-of-capture without drivers needing to check a handheld device.

title: Amazon debuts text-to-shop AI agent feature
gist: Amazon is rolling out a text-based shopping feature for Alexa for Shopping that lets customers add items to cart and complete purchases via SMS, including photo-based product discovery and price tracking. Consumer trust in AI-led purchase completion remains low despite growing usage for research.

title: How Azuna’s strong supply chain fuels its 9-figure sales
gist: DTC air-freshener brand Azuna has reached nine-figure annual online revenue by building supply chain resilience through long-term raw material contracts, owned manufacturing, and multi-tiered fulfillment rather than relying on third-party logistics.

title: Shopping or social? What an under-16 ban could mean for resale
gist: The UK government is weighing whether its proposed under-16 social media ban should extend to online marketplaces like eBay, Vinted, and Depop, whose social features — feeds, messaging, following — blur the line between commerce and social networking. Inclusion could affect both buyer demand and seller supply on resale platforms, and would likely trigger mandatory age verification requirements.

title: AI joins the Christmas ecommerce rush — but will recommendations turn into sales?
gist: Adobe forecasts UK festive online spending to hit £28.52bn, with AI-referred traffic to retail sites up 214% year-on-year during November–December. Consumer research shows AI is primarily used for gift inspiration and price comparison rather than autonomous purchasing, with only 8–19% willing to let AI complete purchases on their behalf.

title: Black Friday spending set to hit £9.8bn as shoppers plan Christmas bargains
gist: UK Black Friday spending is forecast to reach £9.8bn, up 3% year-on-year, with online retail capturing £5.29bn of that. Shopper sentiment has shifted sharply toward viewing Black Friday as a genuine savings event, with 63% calling it a good way to save versus 35% last year.

title: Exclusive: Ulta Beauty bets on health tracking with Oura in 1,000 stores
gist: Ulta Beauty is launching the Oura Ring 5 health tracker across 1,000 U.S. stores and online from mid-November, marking its first foray into wearable health tech. The move is driven by data showing 72% of Ulta's customer base already prioritizes daily wellness.

title: How enterprise brands are retooling commerce platforms to capture AI shoppers
gist: Shopify reports AI-referred traffic to its merchant storefronts up 2.6x year-on-year in Q3, with AI-referred orders up 3.3x and conversion rates 64% higher than organic search. The article argues that winning in agentic commerce requires three things from retailers: structured product data legibility, multi-channel reach, and preserved customer identity through checkout.

title: Beyond the AI shortlist: How brands can inspire the next purchase
gist: As AI agents increasingly build shopping shortlists from structured product data, brands face two distinct challenges: winning the AI recommendation through machine-readable, semantically rich product attributes, and then converting the AI-referred shopper on the product page through visualization, fit confidence, and consistent information. Only 46% of consumers fully trust AI recommendations and 89% double-check before buying.

title: Peak season 2026: What’s changed, and how do you win?
gist: Research from Cardlytics shows UK shoppers are managing budgets tightly even during the festive season, trading down and breaking brand loyalties, but still spending when prompted by relevant, timely offers. The article frames peak 2026 success as a relevance and timing challenge rather than a demand problem.

title: Poundland blocked from buying new stock despite £86m turnaround
gist: Poundland has been blocked from ordering new stock by owner Gordon Brothers, which restricted cash access despite the retailer swinging from an EBITDA loss of £68.1m to a profit of £18.1m in the past year. The company faces administration if a rescue deal isn't secured before its notice of intention to appoint administrators expires on 13 November.

title: Ikea sales fall for third year as it slashes prices to revive growth
gist: Ikea reported a third consecutive year of declining global sales, down 2% to €43.8bn, and is responding with a €1.2bn investment in price cuts of up to 25% across 1,000+ products in Europe alongside a push to open smaller city-centre stores. Weak consumer confidence in China and the Middle East, plus rising freight and energy costs, are cited as ongoing headwinds.

title: Amazon launches AI shopping through text messages in agentic push
gist: Amazon has launched text-based AI shopping through Alexa for Shopping, allowing US customers to search, compare, and purchase products via SMS with the assistant remembering preferences and previous orders. The rollout is part of Amazon's broader agentic commerce push, with agentic feature usage up eightfold since the start of the year.

title: As publishers await click data, Google’s AI visibility push complicates the opt-out decision
gist: Google is developing a Search Console opt-out that lets publishers exclude their content from AI Overviews, following a UK CMA requirement, while simultaneously enhancing AI Overviews to make opting out less commercially attractive. Publishers are waiting for click data to understand the traffic impact before deciding.

title: ChatGPT is about to show brands their mention count
gist: OpenAI is testing an analytics dashboard inside ChatGPT that lets businesses track how often they appear in ChatGPT answers and how many clicks those mentions generate, with a Shopify store connection as one verification route. The tool is part of an unreleased Business Hub that also includes a business agent feature.

title: Exclusive: TikTok Shop launches a paid premium tier for 1M of its top US shoppers
gist: TikTok Shop launched a paid membership pilot called TikTok Shop Plus, offering free shipping, exclusive discounts, and instant refunds for $9.99/month to over 1 million of its most loyal U.S. customers. The move mirrors Amazon Prime and Walmart+ and signals TikTok Shop's push to deepen loyalty as it holds roughly 20% of the U.S. social-commerce market.

title: Reddit is turning user conversations into AI-powered product reviews
gist: Reddit launched 'Reddit Reviews,' an AI-powered feature that aggregates and summarizes user conversations about products into structured review pages covering ~10,000 products, now live for all U.S. users. The feature is designed to position Reddit as a product research destination ahead of the holiday season, though it may also attract brand astroturfing.

title: Singles Day spend set to top £2.2bn as UK shoppers embrace global retail event
gist: UK consumers are forecast to spend over £2.2bn during Singles Day 2025, up roughly 10% year over year, as the event grows beyond its Chinese origins and increasingly marks the start of the UK peak shopping season. Retailers including ASOS, AliExpress, and Temu are extending promotions beyond November 11 into multi-week campaigns.

title: Target vs. Walmart: Holiday marketing’s stakes feel higher this year
gist: Walmart and Target are both anchoring their 2025 holiday campaigns around narrative storytelling rather than pure price messaging, as both retailers compete for the same value-conscious but higher-income shopper. Analysts note Target is leaning into personalization and a unified creator/influencer strategy as its key differentiator against Walmart's scale.

title: Holiday hiring looks different this year. Here’s why.
gist: Retailers are quietly scaling back large seasonal hiring announcements, instead relying on existing staff, on-demand pools, and part-time roles — with Amazon as the notable outlier, planning to hire 300,000+ seasonal workers, up 20% from recent years. The shift from seasonal to part-time labels suggests some employers expect demand to persist well beyond Q4.

title: The Children’s Place, in search of new ownership, files for bankruptcy
gist: The Children's Place filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy with over $881 million in debts, citing declining demand, inflation, tariffs, and intensifying competition from Target, Walmart, and Amazon in value-priced children's apparel. The company is running store-closing sales while seeking a buyer by year-end, with bids due December 9.
